reason: Reproduced exactly, on both grounds at 390 and 1440. Seeded three moments on the primary date (2026-10-03) in record order Wedding day / Ceremony at St John's / Drinks in the walled garden / Dinner and speeches and rendered state=day: .b-dayNowTitle comes back Ceremony at St John's / Dinner and speeches / Drinks in the walled garden / Wedding day under the heading 'Happening today', identical in paper and ink at both widths. Dinner before drinks. render-b.js:2008 is the ONLY .sort() with localeCompare anywhere in the artifact; every other list sorts by day distance (ahead() at :74, place() at :284). I tried the two refutations offered and both fail. (1) 'No time field, so this is a data-model build.' The model is date-only, true — but the proposed fix does not need a time. Dropping the sort falls back to record order, and record order is ALREADY what every other surface prints: driven with the same seed, state=phone, desk, print and owner-flight all render those four in DOM and visual order Wedding day / Ceremony / Drinks / Dinner, because their day-distance sorts are stable and ties keep array order. So this is not 'order by time we don't have', it is 'state=day is the one surface that overrides the tie-break the rest of the product uses'. The concrete failure is a contradiction, not a missing feature: the printed keepsake and the phone screen hand the venue one running order and the wedding-morning screen hands them a different one for the same four moments. Fixing it changes three lines of render code and touches no schema. (2) 'Alphabetical is a deliberate, defensible choice for untimed same-date items.' Nothing supports that. The block carries a long comment defending the count and defending why a second same-day moment renders at all, and says nothing about the sort; no lock.md decision, no SETTLED entry, and no gate assertion mentions it; and the heading over it is a temporal claim. Record order is also author-touched, not incidental: delete/undo re-inserts by index (:1296-1308) precisely to preserve it. SETTLED has no entry for day-screen ordering or for the accessor omission. Second defect confirmed and it is the worse one. With one moment carrying title '' seeded alongside the four, .b-dayNowTitle returns five nodes and the empty one measures height 0 — an invisible paragraph, sorted to the TOP by localeCompare, on all four ground/width combinations. That state is reachable and is the product's designed state, not an edge case: 'add' mints { title: '' } at :1332 and setTitle at :881 persists value.trim(), so '' survives; nameOf at :47 exists for exactly this, its comment claims it is used by 'the row, the accessible name, every receipt and the editor', and interaction-check.mjs:1608-1610 already ASSERTS a freshly added moment reads 'Untitled moment' in the row, the grab label and the panel. states.day:2024 prints m.title raw and is the single place that escapes it, so a moment the owner added but never named is counted by the plural branch and rendered as nothing on the one screen the day is run from. That is the silent-content-deletion class on the highest-stakes surface in the set. Both halves are real, specific, three lines, and within scope.
sharpenedFix: Take the seat's fix as written — :2006-2008 drop the .sort() entirely, :2024 text: nameOf(m) — with one sharpening to the claim and one to the gate. Do not describe the result as 'the order they happen'; the record carries no time and cannot promise that. Describe it as what it measurably is: state=day stops overriding the tie-break, so the morning screen agrees with the printed sheet and the phone. Write the gate assertion as cross-surface agreement rather than as record order, because that is the stronger and more durable property: seed three moments on the primary date in deliberately non-alphabetical record order plus one with title '', then assert (a) the .b-dayNowTitle sequence on state=day is element-for-element identical to the same date's .b-title sequence on state=print and on state=phone, and (b) no .b-dayNowTitle is empty and none measures 0px high — both at 390 and 1440, paper and ink. Assertion (a) fails today on all four combinations and would also catch a future surface that reintroduces its own ordering; assertion (b) fails today and pins the accessor. If the founder later adds a time to the model, (a) still holds and needs no rewrite.
